Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:47: And in the secret of the threads, which are thirty-two, he said that they correspond to the thirty-two paths of Chokhmah, and they emerge through the Righteous One [Yesod] - this is "from the wing of the earth," and so on, "glory to the righteous" (Isaiah 24:16). And this does not contradict the earlier teachings we copied from Rashbi, which indicate that they are in the living creatures - for the thirty-two paths emerge from above through the Righteous One, and spread into one living creature on each side.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:48: And incidentally it is proven there that one should not recite the Shema without tzitzit, along the lines of what they said in the Talmud (Berachot 14b) about one who recites the Shema without tefillin - and this is their wording, on the end of the verse that says (Isaiah 24:16), "woe is me, the treacherous have dealt treacherously," and so on: and when I look at the techelet and see the strap for striking the place of fear, to instill fear, I say, woe is me, that people do not know to pay attention and observe for what they are punished, to deal falsely in this - "the treacherous have dealt treacherously" - for they recite the Shema without tzitzit and bear false testimony, and these are the treacherous who deal falsely with themselves, and "with utter treachery have the treacherous dealt" - their garment without tzitzit is called "the garment of the treacherous" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:49: And it was necessary, from the doubling of the verse saying "the treacherous have dealt treacherously" and "with utter treachery have the treacherous dealt," to say that these are two aspects: the first, one who recites the Shema without tzitzit; and the second, one who has no tzitzit on his garment even not at the time of reciting the Shema - for a person is obligated to have tzitzit upon him the entire day. And they said in the Talmud (Pesachim 113b) that one who has no tzitzit on his garment is like one excommunicated, in these words: our Rabbis taught, eight are as though excommunicated from Heaven, and these are they: one who has no wife; one who has a wife but no children by her and does not divorce her; one who has children but does not raise them to Torah study; one who has no tefillin on his head and arm, and no tzitzit on his garment, and no mezuzah on his doorpost; and one who withholds shoes from his feet; and some say, also one who does not recline at a gathering for a commandment - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:50: And it is impossible to be exempted from this by wearing tzitzit only at the time of prayer, for the time for tzitzit is the whole day, like tefillin and mezuzah - except that since tefillin require a clean body, people refrained from wearing them except at the time of prayer. But the early Tanna'im, peace be upon them - Rabbi Eliezer the Great was careful to wear them all day, even when he was ill, as is proven in Sanhedrin (68a), and likewise our holy Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi], as is proven in Ketubot (104a). And at the end of "The Borrower" chapter of Shabbat (153a) our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said - and these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer - another interpretation (Ecclesiastes 9:8), "let your garments always be white" - this is tzitzit; "and let your head lack no oil" - this is tefillin - to this point. Behold, the obligation is that a person have tzitzit and tefillin the whole day.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:51: And so it became customary to wear a small tallit [tallit katan] all day, and one who has a clean body is obligated to wear tefillin even not at the time of prayer, for they said that he is like one excommunicated, and the reason is that he appears to be casting off the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:52: And in the Sifrei it is said: beloved is Israel, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, surrounded with commandments - tefillin on their heads, tefillin on their arms, tzitzit on their garments, mezuzah on their doorposts - and concerning them David said (Psalms 119:164), "seven times a day I praise You." He entered the bathhouse and saw himself naked, and said, woe is me that I am naked of commandments; when he looked at the [mark of] circumcision, he began to compose praise about it, as it is said (Psalms 6:1), "for the leader, on the eighth [instrument]." A parable of a king of flesh and blood who said to his wife, adorn yourself with all kinds of jewelry so that you may be pleasing to me - so the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, be distinguished with commandments so that you may be pleasing before Me. And so it says (Song of Songs 6:4), "you are beautiful, my love, as Tirzah" - you are beautiful to Me if you are pleasing [ratzui] to Me - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:53: And concerning the virtue of tzitzit, they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Shelach, page 163b) that one who wears tzitzit becomes "whole" [tamim], and concerning him it is said (Deuteronomy 18:13), "you shall be whole" - in these words: along these lines, a person who wears tzitzit becomes every day "whole" - "tam" through the four corners being properly arranged, "yam" [sea] through that techelet of the fish of the seventy levels of the sea - the evil side, when it looks at this person, cannot harm him with the evil eye, and then he is truly "tam-yam" with YHVH his God in one single repair - she above and he below; afterward she ascends among the supernal levels, so too the person afterward ascends, through the tefillin, among the supernal levels, and therefore "you shall be whole with YHVH your God" - with Him, truly, in one time, in one moment, she is repaired above and the person is repaired below - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:54: And further, among the virtues of tzitzit is that its property is to draw the Shechinah to dwell with him, as it is written (Numbers 15:38), "and they shall make for themselves tzitzit on the corners of their garments throughout their generations [le-dorotam]" - and it is as though it said "le-diratam" [for their dwelling], as they expounded in the Tikkunim (page 22b) concerning (Exodus 31:16), "to observe the Sabbath throughout their generations" - see there, whose wording we copy below. And therefore they said, of blessed memory (Menachot 43b), that whoever is careful with the commandment of tzitzit merits to greet the countenance of the Shechinah - "it is written here," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:55: And concerning whether the wrapping in tzitzit precedes tefillin or not, there are clear proofs in the Zohar and the Tikkunim that the wrapping of tzitzit on the head precedes tefillin. First, in the Zohar (Parashat Bamidbar, page 120b), where it is explained that there are four things in deed and, corresponding to them, four in speech - and it says: the first, to purify himself, meaning that he should relieve his body; afterward he should accept upon himself this yoke, to spread over his head the separation of the commandment; afterward he should bind the binding of unification, which is the tefillin - what is tefillin? The tefillah of the head and of the hand, and so on - to this point, relevant here. And in the Tikkunim (page 130b), in these words: come and see, when a person wraps himself in the wrapping of the commandment, and lays tefillin, and recites the Shema, behold he has established for Him a throne through the wrapping of the commandment, and this is as established (Isaiah 16:5), "and it shall be established in kindness, a throne" - and through the tefillin he crowns Him, this is what is written (Ezekiel 24:17), "bind your headdress upon you," and He calls the one who rests upon the throne that he has established for Him "Shema Yisrael" - thus the Holy One, blessed be He, establishes for him, in that world, a throne and a crown - to this point. And a person does not fulfill his obligation properly by wearing a small tallit beneath his clothing, to fulfill the words of these teachings, but only by spreading the commandment of tzitzit over his head, which is what is called "wrapping."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:56: And concerning the placing of the tallit, I have seen those who are precise about the tzitziyot that originally came to the side of the head, that they should always remain on the side of the head - since they merited to be elevated, it is not fitting that they descend from their elevation - and so all Ashkenazim practice, and most of the people of Italy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:57: And concerning the intent of the blessing "to wrap oneself in tzitzit," it is fitting to intend that the soul is what wraps itself in the light of this commandment, both below and above - that the root of the soul, which is above, also wraps itself in the light of this commandment, in aspects to be explained. And this is a general rule for every commandment a person performs: he must intend that his soul, which is a portion of God from above, is repaired and illuminated by the light of this commandment - and likewise concerning tefillin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:58: And I heard from my teacher, peace be upon him, that the intent of "wrapping oneself in tzitzit" is based on what they said, of blessed memory (Bamidbar Rabbah 18:21), that tzitzit numerically equals the six hundred thirteen commandments that are in the Shechinah, in her aspect clothed in the Throne and in Metatron, in which is the secret of tzitzit. And according to what was explained, that the intent of the wrapping is for the soul, one must intend that in his soul there are two hundred forty-eight spiritual limbs and three hundred sixty-five spiritual sinews, and all of them shine through the commandment of tzitzit. And so he explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 227a), that the secret of tzitzit is Metatron, in these words: Metatron, six steps to the throne, which total six hundred; "tzitzit" with two yuds, and if the yud is missing, then a chirik takes its place - so it totals, on every side, in the four corners of the tzitzit, and the thirteen windings of the tzitzit, six hundred thirteen - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:59: And in the book Tola'at Ya'akov (Sod HaTzitzit), he explained how the six hundred thirteen are found in the tzitzit, and wrote, in these words: and this commandment is equal to all the commandments, because it is the first stone that comprises the six hundred thirteen precious stones and the thirty-two paths, and each and every path divides into two, good and evil, "remember" and "observe," a positive commandment and a negative commandment - behold, these are sixty-four, and each one comprises ten sefirot, totaling six hundred forty; subtract from them the twenty-seven letters of the Torah [including the five final forms], and behold, these are the six hundred thirteen commandments of the Torah. And this is what they said, of blessed memory, in the chapter "The Techelet" (Menachot 43b), "and you shall see it and remember all the commandments of the LORD" (Numbers 15:39) - the commandment of tzitzit is equal to all the commandments together - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:60: There are many more matters in the allusion of this commandment, and we have explained only what is relevant in practice to the intent of the blessing and to the matter of handling the tzitziyot - and what is relevant in practice is that, since their allusion is thirty-two corresponding to the thirty-two paths, or as explained above, it is fitting to separate each one individually, and likewise when one handles them he should direct his intent to the secrets alluded to.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:61: And concerning the tefillin, we have already said that their secret is for the purification of thoughts and the drawing of holiness, as they are called "holiness" in the language of our Rabbis, of blessed memory. And in the Midrash HaNe'elam (Parashat Chayei Sarah, page 129a) they said that concerning the secret of tefillin it is said (Exodus 25:8), "and let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them" - in these words: he and Rabbi Yesa and Rabbi Chiya arose and went, and found Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon revealing secrets concerning tefillin - they came before him and said, what is our master engaged with? He said to them, I am telling the reason for tefillin, for happy is the person who lays tefillin and knows their reason. They said, if it please our master, let him tell us something. He said, I heard from my father, that the Holy One, blessed be He, out of the great love He had for Israel, said to them, make Me a Tabernacle in the manner of the supernal Chariot above, and let My dwelling come with them - this is what is written, "and let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them" - and I heard from my father that here, in this verse, is hidden the reason for tefillin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:62: Come and see, in the supernal manner a sanctuary is made through His holy chariots, and afterward the Holy One, blessed be He, causes His dwelling to rest with them - along this same matter and manner, the colleagues, masters of the mishnah, aroused themselves concerning the reason for tefillin, that this person become the pattern of the supernal chariots, a lower chariot and an upper chariot, so that His kingship come upon him and His dwelling rest upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:63: And we have learned, there are supernal secrets and their patterns in it, and there are three chariots, patterns of the supernal holy ones, secrets of the three letters of the holy names of the worlds - three chariots, three letters, four passages ruling over the four - and concerning this is the secret of the "shin" of three crowns and the "shin" of four crowns. Three kings rule in the body, and the tefillin are over them - the Holy One, blessed be He, above - these are the head-tefillin. The arm-tefillin has four passages, the heart rides, as the pattern of the lower chariot, and the lower rides. We have learned further, this is the rider of the arm below, and the heart rides as its pattern, being below, and are delivered into his hand to be tortured, all the hosts of heaven; so the heart rides below and all the limbs of the body are delivered into its hand, and above them are the four passages upon the brain of the head - but the Holy One, blessed be He, is the supernal ruler, King over all. And the secret of this wisdom is like the pattern of the sanctuary, as it is written (Exodus 28:19 - actually the cherubim verse), "and make one cherub on one end, and one cherub on the other end," and upon them is the dwelling of the King in the four letters, two chariots, and in this manner the heart and the brain, the heart on one side and the brain on the other, and upon them is the dwelling of the Holy One, blessed be He, in the four, the four passages. Rabbi Elazar said, from here onward are the secrets of the crowns of the letters, and the passages in their bodies, and their straps - a law given to Moses at Sinai, and their allusion is revealed, and the reason for all is in the thirteen measures of mercy. Rabbi Yehudah said, even if I had come into this world only for this secret, it would be enough for me - to this point. And behold, it is explained in this teaching that tefillin are vessels for causing the Shechinah to rest upon us, for they are the pattern of the supernal cherubim upon whom the Shechinah used to rest.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:64: And they said in the Midrash (Shocher Tov, Psalms 1): Rabbi Eliezer said, Israel said before the Omnipresent, we wish to toil in Torah day and night, but we have no leisure. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, fulfill the commandment of tefillin and I shall account it to you as though you toiled day and night. Rabbi Yochanan said, it is an explicit verse (Exodus 13:9), "and it shall be for a sign upon your hand," and so on, "so that the Torah of the LORD may be in your mouth" - to this point. Behold, the virtue of one who lays tefillin is great, as though he were occupied with Torah, and it is known that Torah study is equal to all the commandments, as it says (Peah, chapter 1, mishnah 1), "and Torah study is equal to them all." And likewise the commandment of tzitzit is equal to them all, as they explained, of blessed memory (Nedarim 25a) - it follows that one who wraps himself in tzitzit and lays tefillin is as though he fulfilled all the commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:65: And so they said in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 101b), in these words: and the holy lamp [Rashbi] said, whoever lays tefillin and tzitzit is as though he fulfilled the six hundred thirteen commandments of the Torah, and not only that, but through tzitzit it is as though he established a throne for the Holy One, blessed be He, and the tefillin are the Name Heh, as though YHVH descended upon the throne - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:66: And in the Tikkunim (page 2a) it says that a person must have, every day, two signs - the sign of the covenant and the sign of tefillin - corresponding to the two yuds in the Name Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh Adonai; and on the Sabbath, the sign of the Sabbath and the sign of the covenant; and whoever does not lay tefillin every day causes separation - and we copied this teaching in the Gate of Love (chapter 9). It follows that as long as tefillin are upon him he is unifying, and the Shechinah rests upon him, since the tefillin are from her side.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:67: Further, in the Tikkunim (end of page 142b), it says that one occupied with Torah while wrapped in tzitzit and tefillin merits nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah, in these words: and therefore Israel must illuminate her [the Shechinah] in exile with light and with a lamp, which is Torah and commandment, the light of the soul - nefesh, ru'ach, whose sign is "ner" [lamp] - in the boxes of the tefillin, so that the Shechinah may find rest in exile through them, and the covering of the tzitzit to wrap herself in it; and therefore, if a person does not lay tefillin and [wear] tzitzit, in what shall she lie down in exile? Concerning this it is said (Psalms 41:2), "happy is he who considers the poor; the LORD will deliver him in the day of trouble." And by the merit of these precepts, people inherit three bonds, which are neshamah, ru'ach, and nefesh. And he said further there, and therefore neshamah, ru'ach, and nefesh are the bed of the Shechinah in exile, and concerning them it is said (Deuteronomy 24:13), "and he shall lie down in his garment and bless you," and because of these precepts the Shechinah rests upon a person.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:68: Behold, it is explained in this teaching that these three commandments - Torah, tefillin, and tzitzit - correspond to neshamah, ru'ach, nefesh, as explained at the beginning of the teaching, which says, "the light of the soul." And Torah too is included among the commandments, being one of the two hundred forty-eight positive commandments, to study Torah, and so on - and since one merits these three, the Shechinah rests upon him, for the Shechinah rests only upon a complete throne, which is these three, as explained at the end of the teaching. And certainly for this reason it was the custom of the early Tanna'im to lay tefillin all day, as I proved above, in order to draw the Shechinah upon them through their being a complete throne, as explained in the teaching.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:69: And so also it says (Berachot 30b): Rabbi Yirmiyah was sitting before Rabbi Zeira, and saw that he was very cheerful. He said to him, does the master not hold (Proverbs 14:23), "in all sorrow there is profit"? Rashi explains, when a person shows himself sorrowful he shall have reward. He said to him, I am wearing tefillin. And Rashi explains, "I am wearing tefillin" - and these are testimony that the dominion of my Maker and His kingship are upon me. And it is difficult to say that this wearing of tefillin was at the time of prayer, for from Rabbi Yirmiyah's saying that he was sitting before Rabbi Zeira, it appears that this was in his study hall, not at the time of prayer. And so, according to the reading of Rabbeinu Yonah, of blessed memory, who reads before this concerning Abaye - he was sitting before Rava and saw that he was very cheerful. He said to him, is it not written (Psalms 2:11), "and rejoice with trembling"? He said to him, I am wearing tefillin. It appears certain that this was not at the time of prayer, for if it had been at the time of prayer, it would be very difficult for these Amoraim - would the mishnah (Berachot chapter 5, mishnah 1) have been hidden from them, "one may only stand to pray in a state of gravity"? And likewise, Rabbi Zeira did not say to Rabbi Yirmiyah, "is it not written, 'rejoice with trembling'?" - for that verse, "rejoice with trembling," proves more concerning the matter of prayer, since from this verse the Talmud earlier derived that one may only stand to pray in a state of gravity, more than from the verse "in all sorrow there is profit." And likewise Rabbi Zeira and Rava did not say, "but we have learned, one may only stand to pray in a state of gravity" - rather, certainly this was not at the time of prayer, for their custom was to wear tefillin all day, even while occupied with Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:70: And concerning what each of them answered, "I am wearing tefillin," the disciples of Rabbeinu Yonah explained, in these words: he means to say, I am rejoicing in the joy of a commandment, for I was ill in my bowels and could not lay tefillin for several days because of concern for cleanliness, and now that I have recovered I rejoice in the fulfillment of this commandment out of my desire for it - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:71: Further, we say in the Talmud (Berachot 23b): Rabbi Yitzchak said, one who enters a fixed meal removes his tefillin and then enters - and this disagrees with Rabbi Chiya, who said, Rabbi Chiya said, he places them on his table, and so they honor him. And until when? Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said, until the time of the blessing. And Rashi explains, "he removes his tefillin," lest he become drunk at the meal and disgrace himself while wearing tefillin. "And so they honor him," so that they are ready for him and he puts them back on at the time of the blessing - to this point. And Rabbeinu Yaakov ruled like Rabbi Chiya (Tur, Orach Chaim, siman 40). And the Rif, of blessed memory: one who enters a fixed meal removes them and places them on the table until the time of the blessing, and puts them back on - to this point. Therefore a person should accustom himself to this commandment of tefillin, to wear them most of the day, and he will merit length of days. In any case, one who wears tefillin all day and is occupied with Torah while wearing them must handle them at all times, so that his mind not stray from them, for our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Menachot 36b), an a fortiori argument from the frontplate, which had only one mention [of the divine Name], and so on - tefillin, which have forty-two [letters/mentions], all the more so.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:72: And if it is impossible for a person to wear them during the day because of concern for the cleanliness of his body, at least at the time of prayer it is fitting to wear them, for at the time of prayer it is fitting to pray with a clean body, since it is forbidden for him to pray if he cannot hold himself for the distance of a parasah, as explained in the Talmud - and since his body is clean for prayer, it is also clean for tefillin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:73: And they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 108b) that the completeness of prayer is in the wrapping of tallit and tefillin, in these words: and if the prayer ascends complete, in the wrapping of the commandment and tefillin on the head and arm, it is said of them (Deuteronomy 28:10), "and all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of the LORD is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you" - "the Name of the LORD," they established, is the head-tefillin, and whoever sees the Name of the LORD upon the head in prayer, which is the Name YHVH, immediately they all flee - this is what is written (Psalms 91:7), "a thousand shall fall at your side," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:74: And further, in the Zohar (Parashat Toldot, page 141a), in these words: and therefore whoever does not wrap himself in this, and is not crowned to be strengthened by tefillin every day, it is as though faithfulness does not rest with him, and the fear of his Master departs from him, and his prayer is not a proper prayer - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:75: And therefore it is fitting that every prayer be with the wrapping of tzitzit and tefillin, except the evening prayer, and the custom has already spread in the Land of Israel to wear tefillin even at the afternoon prayer. And it is fitting to practice this way, because the property of tefillin is to subdue the external forces, as explained in the teaching - and this is one of the intentions that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim, that one who directs his intent must, at the time of laying tefillin, intend to subdue the servant under his master and the maidservant under her mistress - and so he explained in the Tikkunim (page 2a), in these words: mighty ones from the side of Gevurah, who give strength to their masters, to subdue the servant under his master and the maidservant under her mistress through the binding of the tefillin - for whoever has no tefillin at the time of reciting the Shema, from his side the servant and maidservant rule over the world, and at that hour the Shechinah is angered - and this is what is written (Proverbs 30:22), "under a servant when he becomes king, and a maidservant when she supplants her mistress" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:76: And in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu it is said, on the verse (Genesis 32:24), "and Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him" - they said, of blessed memory, this teaches that he wished to kill him, but had no power, because our father Jacob was armed with tefillin on his head and arm and tzitzit on his garment - this is what is written (ibid. 32:25), "and when he saw that he could not prevail against him," and so on - and it is known that this man was the guardian angel of Persia [Esau], as they explained, of blessed memory.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:77: And in the Tikkunim, found elsewhere among us in manuscript (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 106b), the matter is explained further, and there he stated the difference between a servant and a son in performing this commandment, in these words: whoever's soul is from the Tree of Life, certainly when he lays tefillin, it is to bring all the other gods under all the dominion of the supernal Shechinah, which is the head-tefillin of a person, and to bring all nations under the hand of the LORD, which is the lower Shechinah - because in exile it is said (Proverbs 30:21-22), "for three things the earth is troubled... under a servant when he becomes king, and a churl when he is filled with food, and a maidservant when she supplants her mistress" - and therefore, in the head and hand tefillin, one brings the maidservant under her mistress, supernal and lower, and in the inner mentions [of the divine Name] included within them, which are equal to the Torah, one must bring the servant under his master, supernal and lower - and this is called a son of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, this is what is written (Exodus 4:22), "thus says the LORD, Israel is My firstborn son" - and those who do this, of them it is said (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the LORD your God" - and therefore it is said (Avot, chapter 1, mishnah 3), "do not be like servants who serve their master in order to receive a reward." And whoever performs this precept in order to bind the other gods so that they become subjugated, and the nations below, to place them under his hand - they give him a soul only from the side of a servant, and therefore, whether as sons or as servants - to this point. And what he said, "under her mistress, supernal and lower," is the supernal Heh and the lower Heh; and "under his master, supernal and lower," is the Yud and the Vav.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:78: Behold, the intent of tefillin is explained in one manner, and the difference in performing this commandment between a servant and a son - for the son does not intend his own benefit but only what pertains to the honor of his father and mother, and therefore he intends the subjugation of the husks, "the servant under his master and the maidservant under her mistress."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:79: And further, they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 101b) that tefillin, for the intermediate ones [beinonim], have the property of subduing the accusers - it says there, concerning the difference in the performance of the commandments of tzitzit and tefillin between the completely righteous and the intermediate ones, that the righteous intend to establish a throne for the King through the wrapping of tzitzit, and the King who comes to sit upon the throne through the laying of tefillin, as explained above - and it says that from the side of the completely righteous, he is not imprisoned in exile, but is bound and imprisoned with them in love, tied to them in affection, this is what is written (Genesis 44:30), "and his soul is bound up with his soul" - imprisoned with them in the throne prepared for him and in its chariot, and so on - but from the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, which binds them to the good inclination to be a help alongside them, and binds them to the evil inclination to be a burden beneath them, a donkey carrying books. From the side of the intermediate ones, he is imprisoned and bound in exile, of whom it is said, in the days of the week he was bound like an ox for plowing and like a donkey for burden, and on the Sabbath, "so that your ox and your donkey may rest" (Exodus 23:12) - he was like an ox to the yoke, the yoke of tefillin, and like a donkey for burden. Of the wicked it is said (Lamentations 1:14), "the LORD has given me into the hands of those I am unable to withstand" - for the straps of the tefillin are like ropes for the horns of Samael, a goring ox that they do not destroy, and the hand-tefillin is bound to his legs - and whoever does not lay tefillin, of him it is said (Berachot 33a), "keep as far as possible from a goring ox," for from him depend the primary categories of damages; tzitzit is a burden on the donkey - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:80: And they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 108b) that the completeness of prayer is in the wrapping of tallit and tefillin - in these words: and if the prayer ascends complete in the wrapping of the commandment, and tefillin on the head and arm, it is said of them (Deuteronomy 28:10), "and all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of the LORD is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you" - "the Name of the LORD," they established, is the head-tefillin, and whoever sees the Name of the LORD upon the head in prayer, which is the Name YHVH, immediately they all flee - this is what is written (Psalms 91:7), "a thousand shall fall at your side," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:81: And further, in the Zohar (Parashat Toldot, page 141a), in these words: and therefore whoever does not wrap himself in this, and is not crowned to be strengthened by tefillin every day, it is as though faithfulness does not rest with him, and the fear of his Master departs from him, and his prayer is not a proper prayer - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:82: And therefore it is fitting that every prayer be with the wrapping of tzitzit and tefillin, except the evening prayer, and the custom has already spread in the Land of Israel to wear tefillin even at the afternoon prayer. And it is fitting to practice this way, because the property of tefillin is to subdue the external forces, as explained in the teaching - and this is one of the intentions that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim, that one who directs his intent must, at the time of laying tefillin, intend to subdue the servant under his master and the maidservant under her mistress - and so he explained in the Tikkunim (page 2a), in these words: mighty ones from the side of Gevurah, who give strength to their masters, to subdue the servant under his master and the maidservant under her mistress through the binding of the tefillin - for whoever has no tefillin at the time of reciting the Shema, from his side the servant and maidservant rule over the world, and at that hour the Shechinah is angered, and this is what is written (Proverbs 30:22), "under a servant when he becomes king, and a maidservant when she supplants her mistress" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:83: And in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu, on the verse (Genesis 32:24), "and Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him," they said, of blessed memory, this teaches that he wished to kill him, but had no power, because our father Jacob was armed with tefillin on his head and arm and tzitzit on his garment - this is what is written (ibid. 32:25), "and when he saw that he could not prevail against him," and so on - and it is known that this man was the guardian angel of Persia [Esau], as they explained, of blessed memory.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:84: And in the Tikkunim, found elsewhere among us in manuscript (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 106b), the matter is explained further, and there he stated the difference between a servant and a son in performing this commandment, in these words: whoever's soul is from the Tree of Life, certainly when he lays tefillin, it is to bring all the other gods under all the dominion of the supernal Shechinah, which is the head-tefillin of a person, and to bring all nations under the hand of the LORD, which is the lower Shechinah - because in exile it is said (Proverbs 30:21-22), "for three things the earth is troubled... under a servant when he becomes king, and a churl when he is filled with food, and a maidservant when she supplants her mistress" - and therefore, in the head and hand tefillin, one brings the maidservant under her mistress, supernal and lower, and in the inner mentions [of the divine Name] included within them, which are equal to the Torah, one must bring the servant under his master, supernal and lower - and this is called a son of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, this is what is written (Exodus 4:22), "thus says the LORD, Israel is My firstborn son" - and those who do this, of them it is said (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the LORD your God" - and therefore it is said (Avot, chapter 1, mishnah 3), "do not be like servants who serve their master in order to receive a reward." And whoever performs this precept in order to bind the other gods so that they become subjugated, and the nations below, to place them under his hand - they give him a soul only from the side of a servant, and therefore, whether as sons or as servants - to this point. And what he said, "under her mistress, supernal and lower," is the supernal Heh and the lower Heh; and "under his master, supernal and lower," is the Yud and the Vav.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:85: Behold, the intent of tefillin is explained in one manner, and the difference in performing this commandment between a servant and a son - for the son does not intend his own benefit but only what pertains to the honor of his father and mother, and therefore he intends the subjugation of the husks, "the servant under his master and the maidservant under her mistress."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:86: And further, they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 101b) that tefillin, for the intermediate ones [beinonim], have the property of subduing the accusers - it says there, concerning the difference in the performance of the commandments of tzitzit and tefillin between the completely righteous and the intermediate ones, that the righteous intend to establish a throne for the King through the wrapping of tzitzit, and the King who comes to sit upon the throne through the laying of tefillin, as explained above - and it says that from the side of the completely righteous, he is not imprisoned in exile, but is bound and imprisoned with them in love, tied to them in affection, this is what is written (Genesis 44:30), "and his soul is bound up with his soul" - imprisoned with them in the throne prepared for him and in its chariot, and so on - but from the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, which binds them to the good inclination to be a help alongside them, and binds them to the evil inclination to be a burden beneath them, a donkey carrying books. From the side of the intermediate ones, he is imprisoned and bound in exile, of whom it is said, in the days of the week he was bound like an ox for plowing and like a donkey for burden, and on the Sabbath, "so that your ox and your donkey may rest" (Exodus 23:12) - he was like an ox to the yoke, the yoke of tefillin, and like a donkey for burden. Of the wicked it is said (Lamentations 1:14), "the LORD has given me into the hands of those I am unable to withstand" - for the straps of the tefillin are like ropes for the horns of Samael, a goring ox that they do not destroy, and the hand-tefillin is bound to his legs - and whoever does not lay tefillin, of him it is said (Berachot 33a), "keep as far as possible from a goring ox," for from him depend the primary categories of damages; tzitzit is a burden on the donkey - to this point.
